title: Nesting one level below maxDepth expands fully
rationale: The below-the-cliff control leg. Without it, a regression that truncates one level too eagerly would be invisible, because every other depth fixture already expects loss.
catchesBugClass: Off-by-one in the maxDepth comparison, and any change that makes the depth check fire before the level is actually consumed. Also catches accidental array inference on ordinary short strings.
cannotCatch: Nothing about the cliff itself - it is two levels clear. It also cannot catch depth accounting for lists, nor the interaction of depth with empty containers.

predicted.detail: Two map levels, deepest flattenObject runs at depth 1, no truncation; neither value triggers array inference.
